Adroit

uh-DROYT · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Adroit is skillful with hands or mind.

The adroit surgeon completed the delicate procedure in half the expected time.

Worked Example

The adroit negotiator settled the dispute in a single afternoon, satisfying both sides completely without a single raised voice.

Adroit describes someone who handles a task -- physical, mental, or social -- with impressive skill and ease, making it look almost effortless.

Your Turn

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

skillful: Skillful is the broad, everyday word for having real ability at a task -- it says you do something well, and nothing more. Adroit is more particular: it admires deft, clever ease, skill so smooth that the hard part looks almost easy, whether with hands or with words.

nimble: Nimble is about lightness and speed -- quick feet, quick fingers, a mind that leaps from idea to idea. Adroit is about cleverness and control instead: an adroit move can be slow and patient, so long as it is handled with expert ease.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

maladroit: clumsy or unskillful

clumsy: lacking skill or grace

Where it sits · how polished the skill is — capable → adroit → masterful

capable vs. adroit: Being capable just means you can get the job done competently; adroit sits a clear step above, handling even a tricky task with deft, clever ease.

masterful vs. adroit: Masterful goes a step beyond adroit: an adroit worker makes one hard task look easy, while a masterful one shows complete command of the whole craft.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Adroit comes whole from the French phrase à droit, literally "to the right" or "properly" -- it entered English as a single borrowed word, not built from a separate English prefix and root.

Use the root in a new word: direct

Use the root in a new word: direct: Interestingly, French droit ultimately traces back to the same Latin word (directus, "straight") that gives English "direct" -- a fun cross-language echo, even though the two words took very different paths into English.

Word Choice

Adroit is a warm, admiring word for skill -- it works equally well praising a craftsman's hands or a diplomat's clever handling of a tense conversation.
